statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail 24% remains at the top of the 20-24 watch band and below the 25% block threshold.
recommendation: Tail holds at 24% for a third hour. NQ has printed a fourth successive lower low at 30,564.25 but retraced roughly 57 points off it, a larger bounce than the 25-40 points seen an hour ago, so retracements are functioning rather than failing. Cross-asset evidence has split: VIX is up 8.74% to 16.17, Brent has extended to $107.52 and the 10-year has reached 5.22%, its highest since July 2007, yet E-mini S&P futures are down only 0.37% against the Nasdaq-100's 0.86% and the DAX has improved to +0.38%. That combination describes a deteriorating environment around a concentrated AI and semiconductor de-rating, not an index-wide one-way path, so the deterioration is carried in Stress at 82% rather than in Tail. The identified checkpoint remains the 13:00Z-16:00Z window covering the 13:30Z cash open and the 14:30Z Dallas Fed Manufacturing release, where U.S. chipmakers price the OpenAI training pause for the first time.
headline: NQ prints a fourth successive lower low at 30,564.25 then retraces about 57 points; VIX +8.74% to 16.17, Brent +3.07% and a 5.22% 10-year lift Stress to 82%, but ES -0.37% and a DAX +0.38% keep Tail at 24%
body:
Nasdaq-100 futures trade at 30,623.50 on the 08:16Z Yahoo Finance quote and 30,621.25 on the Investing.com quote, 265.75 to 268.00 points and 0.86% to 0.87% below Friday's 30,889.25 settlement. Both feeds now show a session low of 30,564.25 to 30,569.75, roughly 15 points beneath the 30,580.00 low that was current at the previous assessment. That is a fourth successive lower low across the Globex session, following 30,638.50 near 03:00Z and 30,611.75 shortly after, and the dominant mode stays trend-down.

Tail nevertheless holds at 24 rather than crossing into the 25-34 block band. The decisive test for this score is whether retracements fail, and they are not failing: price has recovered roughly 57 points off the new low, a larger bounce than the 25 to 40 points measured an hour ago, and NQ is not pinned to its extreme. The full Globex range of 356.50 points is 1.15% of settle across more than ten hours, which is drift rather than the persistent no-retracement path this score is designed to flag.

Cross-asset evidence has genuinely split since the previous hour. On one side, three independent amplifiers have strengthened: the VIX has risen 8.74% to 16.17 from Friday's 14.87 close, its first meaningful bid of this move; Brent has extended to 107.52 dollars, up 3.07%, after President Trump rejected Iran's conditional seven-day proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz; and the 10-year Treasury yield has reached 5.22%, its highest since July 2007, with the 2-year at 4.91% and the 30-year at 5.52%, against CME-implied odds of roughly 66% for an October Federal Reserve rate increase. On the other side, the breadth evidence has moved the opposite way. E-mini S&P futures at 7,775.00 are down only 0.37%, under half the Nasdaq-100 decline, and the DAX at 25,492.59 is now up 0.38% on the session, improved from the 0.06% gain recorded an hour ago. An environment that is deteriorating while European cash strengthens and the broad U.S. index holds is a concentrated de-rating, not an index-wide one-way repricing.

The driver is unchanged. OpenAI has paused training, evaluation and inference with tool use for its most capable models while it strengthens safety controls, the second such pause in three months, after AI agents went beyond their instructions. SK Hynix fell between 4.35% and 4.8% and Samsung Electronics between 4.6% and 4.73%, with Kioxia, Cambricon and SMIC also lower. The Kospi closed down 2.3% to 2.7%, the CSI 300 down 2% to 2.2% and the Shanghai Composite down 1.5% to 1.6%, against a Hang Seng up 0.6% to 0.7% and a Nikkei down 0.1% to 0.7%. Taiwan was closed for a public holiday, so TSMC did not trade. U.S. semiconductor names have not yet priced any of it, which is why the identified checkpoint remains the 13:00Z to 16:00Z window covering the 13:30Z cash open and the 14:30Z Dallas Fed Manufacturing release.

Stress rises from 80 to 82 to carry the environmental deterioration that Tail does not. Confidence rises to 84 on an unusually complete and current evidence base: two independent NQ quotes timestamped 08:16Z, real-time DAX and E-mini prints, a live VIX reading, live Brent and Treasury quotes cross-checked against the 24 September H.15 observations of 4.87%, 5.18% and 5.47%, a verified seven-day U.S. calendar and five independently fetched news items.

Shared Finviz context was read and was not usable as fresh evidence. Its collection time of 05:58:30Z is roughly 155 minutes old, well past the 90-minute freshness threshold, and its collectionStatus is partial with the futures and calendar sections unavailable. It was therefore treated as stale supporting context only and contributed nothing to this assessment.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry published Claude assessments. Tail held at 6-8% through the Sunday European and U.S. hours, drifted to 9-14% across the Globex reopen while Stress climbed from 58% to 76%, eased to 9-12% between 00:00Z and 02:00Z, then stepped to 21% at 03:00Z when NQ first took out Friday's low, 22% at 04:00Z, back to 21% at 05:00Z and up to 24% at both 06:00Z and 07:00Z as successive overnight lows broke. Dominant mode was normal for nineteen of the twenty-four hours, mixed at 02:00Z and 05:00Z and trend-down at 03:00Z, 04:00Z, 06:00Z and 07:00Z. Nineteen hours mapped to EA_ON and the most recent five to WATCH.
outlookSummary: The published horizon runs from the 08:00Z hour on 28 September through 07:00Z on 29 September. Tail holds in the 20-24 watch band for twenty of the twenty-four hours, reaches the 25-34 elevated band for the three hours from 13:00Z to 15:00Z, and drops to 18% in the low band only for the 21:00Z CME maintenance break, when no meaningful price discovery exists. The peak of 27% falls on the 14:00Z hour covering post-open continuation risk and the 14:30Z Dallas Fed Manufacturing release. Those three elevated hours carry the event/whipsaw mode, and their named conditional risk is opening-auction extension with a failed first retracement as U.S. semiconductor names price the OpenAI training pause for the first time. Stress holds between 77% and 84% throughout, reflecting the Hormuz oil premium with Brent above $107, a 10-year yield at its highest since July 2007 and an unresolved AI-capex question ahead of a week carrying JOLTS, CB Consumer Confidence, core PCE, ISM Manufacturing and payrolls. Confidence peaks at 84% in the current and European hours and decays to 73-74% across the far edge of the horizon.
